conclusion.justification: The report explicitly concludes that widespread mask wearing reduces COVID-19 infections, citing multiple studies including systematic reviews and a randomized trial to support this conclusion. Therefore, it endorses the claim.

report:
## Conclusion

The evidence indicates **yes**—when a large proportion of the population wears masks, COVID-19 infections are reduced. Your initial answer of "no" is not supported by the available research.

## Key Evidence

1. **A 2022 PNAS study** directly examined population-level mask wearing (not just mandates) and found that mean mask-wearing levels corresponded to a **19% decrease** in SARS-CoV-2 transmission. ([https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.2119266119](https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.2119266119))

2. **A 2025 systematic review in MDPI** concluded that "masking policies and mask wearing are beneficial to prevent and reduce the risk of SARS-CoV-2 infections and COVID-19 disease in various real-world settings." ([https://www.mdpi.com/1660-4601/22/10/1590](https://www.mdpi.com/1660-4601/22/10/1590))

3. **A landmark PNAS evidence review** cited a WHO-sponsored systematic review by Chu et al. finding that "face mask use could result in a large reduction in risk of infection," and synthesized broader literature supporting population-level impact. ([https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.2014564118](https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.2014564118))

4. **The Bangladesh randomized cluster trial** (summarized by The Conversation) found COVID-19 fell by **35% for people 60+** and **23% for people 50–60** in villages where masks were promoted, with a 12% reduction in COVID-19-like symptoms overall. ([https://theconversation.com/evidence-shows-that-yes-masks-prevent-covid-19-and-surgical-masks-are-the-way-to-go-167963](https://theconversation.com/evidence-shows-that-yes-masks-prevent-covid-19-and-surgical-masks-are-the-way-to-go-167963))

## Summary

Multiple lines of evidence—systematic reviews, a randomized controlled trial, and population-level observational studies—converge on the conclusion that widespread mask wearing reduces SARS-CoV-2 transmission at the population level. The effect is modest but meaningful at the community scale, and more pronounced for higher-quality masks (surgical vs. cloth) and among older age groups.
